# Introduction {.unnumbered}

**Unit 1: Where AI Came From**

We start with a question: what is AI? Then we follow its story from the 1950s to ChatGPT. You will see the big dreams, the big failures, and the moments that changed everything.

Every lesson adds cards to a **class timeline** on the wall. You will play with the same ideas the scientists tried: a chatbot made of rules, a game bot, and pictures that need labels.

***

## What You'll Learn

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

* Explain how AI is different from a normal computer program
* Tell the story of AI from the 1950s to today
* Explain why AI built on rules did not work well for seeing and language
* Explain why data and fast computer chips changed AI
* Name the people and moments that changed AI

***

## Topics in This Unit

[**What Is AI?**](1.1_What_Is_AI.qmd)\
Sort things into AI and not AI, try to write a rule for “cat,” and play a drawing game against an AI.

[**Can a Machine Think?**](1.2_Can_a_Machine_Think.qmd)\
Learn Alan Turing's question from 1950. Play his imitation game with a real AI.

[**The First Chatbot**](1.3_The_First_Chatbot.qmd)\
Be ELIZA with paper. Then chat with ELIZA, read its rules, and add your own.

[**Rules Win at Games**](1.4_Rules_Win_at_Games.qmd)\
Big promises, AI winters, and a chess computer. Play a tic-tac-toe bot and turn off its rules.

[**Data Changes Everything**](1.5_Data_Changes_Everything.qmd)\
Fei-Fei Li, ImageNet, and the big win of 2012. Label pictures like the ImageNet workers did.

[**Transformers and ChatGPT**](1.6_Transformers_and_ChatGPT.qmd)\
Attention, GPT, and Nobel Prizes for AI. Build a sentence one vote at a time, then finish the class timeline.
